summary: Batch job billed at chat rate after tool-call fallback; EU currency rounding removed provisional credits
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a ~€9,300 charge on finalized invoice for a long-running batch-embed job. The job was expected to be billed under batch pricing (per-batch rate) but appears to have been charged at the chat/streaming per-token rate for a ~12-hour run. In addition, a €210 provisional credit for a scheduled kv-cache warmup was missing from the finalized invoice; the customer says the credit was visible in the billing preview before finalize.

Impact:
- LuminaDocs reports a one-off ~€9,300 unexpected charge (customer-visible line item) and a missing provisional credit of €210. Total delta ≈ €9,510.
- Customer is enterprise, in EU (eu-west) private deployment, and is now asking for a credit and root cause to avoid revoking autopay.

Environment:
- Private deployment connected to Redwood control plane (private fallback enabled).
- Primary job submitted from LuminaDocs org via dedicated endpoint; when capacity was low, traffic routed to hosted fallback in eu-west.
- Job invoked tool-calls in streaming responses to serialize metadata; original job type: batch-embedding (async job) with large microbatches.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Submit large async batch job for 1,200 documents using embed pipeline with tool-call metadata serializer enabled.
2) During peak, dedicated pool saturated -> requests routed to hosted fallback using fallback model variant.
3) Hosted runtime treats incoming requests as streaming/chat due to tool-call header and the model variant capability flags; meter records tokens under streaming/chat rate-class.
4) Invoice finalized on next billing cycle; provisional credit for scheduled cache warmup was not applied due to currency rounding logic that reclassified small credits after conversion to EUR.

Logs / attachments provided by customer:
- billing_line_item_2026-02-28.pdf (customer copy)
- job-uuid-3f9b7f-log.txt (contains routing headers and fallback decision timestamp)
- sample-request-headers.json (shows X-Redwood-Tool-Call: true and X-Job-Mode: batch)
comments: 2026-03-12 — Asha Menon (Support): Acknowledged receipt and escalated to Billing + Routing. Asked for full invoice PDF and job UUIDs. SLA 4 business days noted.

2026-03-13 — Diego Alvarez (Billing): Reproduced exported invoice lines from the meter. Observed that the hosted fallback generated meter tags 'rate_class:streaming' for a subset of requests between 03:22-03:35 UTC. Requested infra traces for routing decisions.

2026-03-13 — SRE (automated): Link to trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/0f5a9c — shows dedicated pool saturated at 03:20 UTC; routing policy fallback triggered to hosted eu-west. Kernel selection differences noted (fallback variant set 'supports_streaming:true').

2026-03-13 — LuminaDocs (Customer): Provided signed invoice PDF and confirmed they used the 'metadata-tool' toggle for serialization. Customer requests a provisional credit and refund for misbilled tokens if confirmed.

2026-03-14 — Diego Alvarez (Billing): Preliminary hypothesis: tool-call header + fallback variant capability caused meter classifier to mark requests as streaming. Also uncovered a rounded-currency reconciliation rule that drops credits below €1 after conversion then re-applies smoothing during finalize; that logic suppressed the €210 provisional credit under certain exchange-rate snapshots. Eng investigating patch for classifier and reconciliation edgecase.
investigation_notes:
Investigation summary:
- Routing: At 03:20 UTC dedicated pool reached saturation. Smart routing selected hosted eu-west pool as fallback (expected behavior).
- Model variant selection: Fallback chose a variant flagged 'supports_streaming' because it offered lower-latency kernel for small sequences. The presence of X-Redwood-Tool-Call and streaming-capable variant led the meter classifier to route token accounting into 'streaming/chat' buckets rather than 'batch' buckets.
- Metering classifier: Token classification is feature-gated; current gate logic prioritized 'tool-call=true' over 'job.mode=batch'. This was intentional historically for interactive workloads but is incorrect for async batch jobs that include tool-call metadata.
- Currency rounding: The bill preview uses a short-running FX snapshot; finalization uses EOD FX and applies a smoothing rule that eliminates sub-euro provisional credits if total credit < €2 after re-aggregation. The €210 was above threshold, but due to an earlier rounding bug in aggregator, the kv-cache warmup credit was split across two micro-lines, each < €1 after conversion and subsequently dropped.
- Repro: We replayed a sanitized client request (same headers) in staging with dedicated saturation simulated; the meter logged 'rate_class:streaming' for chunks originating from requests that contained tool-call headers.

Next steps:
- Immediate: create provisional credit adjustment and one-off invoice correction for LuminaDocs (billing).
- Short-term fix: Update metering classifier to prefer job.mode=batch for async jobs where job metadata indicates batch semantics even if tool-call flag is present; roll canary in staging and eu-west hosted pools. (ENG-3210)
resolution_notes:
Workarounds and resolution plan:
1) Temporary credit: Issued provisional credit of €9,510 to LuminaDocs account pending formal invoice adjustment. (Billing actioned 2026-03-14)
2) Patch: Metering classifier change submitted (PR github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-service/pull/872) to bias toward job.mode when present. Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-16 to eu-west hosted fallback pools. Linked INT follow-up for private deployment docs update.
3) Currency reconciliation: Filed bug with finance team to stop splitting small credits across micro-lines during FX conversion (FIN-452). A hotfix will prevent sub-euro line splitting during finalize.
4) Communication: Drafted customer-facing message explaining the root cause, the immediate credit, and planned fixes. Offered LuminaDocs a 3-month billing guard (manual review) for enterprise trust.

Status: provisional credit applied; engineering patch in review. Pending post-canary verification (due 2026-03-20) and final invoice reissue.
